## What is a multimedia presentation?

- In the context of this class (and most science) we use the term "multimedia" to describe dissemination that is **not** flat (i.e., not intended to be read from start-to-finish)
    - might involve a narrator
    - might involve interactivity
    - might involve animations <br><br>
    
- The future of scientific dissemination?

## Some example dissemination tools

1. "Chalk Talk"
2. Slide Deck 
    - PowerPoint, Canva, Markdown
3. Live Demonstrations
4. Video Presentations
    - Screen recordings
    - Explainer videos / cartoons
5. Podcast and audio recordings

## What type of presentation should you make?

- Depends
    - Presentation-style
        - Live or asynchronous? Collaborative?
    - Resources
        - Is there a projector? is there a chalkboard?
    - Content
        - technical, visual/symbolic, chronological story
    - Audience
        - novice to expert

## Getting started with Quarto

- Quarto is a markdown-variant that allows you to create pdf and html presentations, especially useful if you are trying to integrate source code in your presentation<br><br>

- Uses text-based tags that create a new "slide", lists, add figures and links <br><br>

- Easy to create Quarto presentations in RStudio<br><br>

## Screen recording 

- Pragmatic to record your whole screen, allowing you to use any presentation software you like (e.g., Canva, HTML) and have flexibility with your demonstrations<br><br>

- Several tools for recording screen:
  - Video conferencing tool (e.g., Zoom, MS Teams)
  - Clipchamp is a Microsoft365 product that supports short recordings (< 10 minutes)
  - OBS Studio
  
::: {.notes}
- show recording a screen with clipchamp
- show my set up with OBS
:::

## Sharing Videos

- Multimedia presentations can be very large files; hard to distribute through email and Blackboard<br><br>

- Can leverage cloud storage services to **share the link** to a multimedia file that is stored in your cloud
  - Key is to make sure you set correct permissions so your audience can access your file<br><br>

- In this class, I recommend you export your data presentation (MA3) as an *mp4* video files and upload them to your One Drive; share a link to your video presentation in your submission on Blackboard
